Question Choices: Find all zeros of x^3 - 9x by factoring. Enter them in increasing order.
Solution: Factor x^3-9x=x*(x - 3)*(x + 3). Remove the common monomial first, then factor any remaining difference of squares. Do not divide away a factor x and lose the zero at 0. Set each factor to zero. The distinct zeros in order are -3, 0, 3. Repeated factors do not create new distinct zeros.

Hints: Group the first two and last two terms.;Factor (x + 3)(x^2 - 4).
